charts.title: LSTM size at nominal noise
charts.subtitle: 36/36 evaluated models · 2,196/2,196 model/settings · 1,024 trials per setting · snapshot 2026-11-18T09:47:07+00:00
charts.caption: P_L(50) at σq/L = 0.20, σm/L = 0.05, ρ = 0.90. Each cell is one independently trained model. Pointwise 95% Wilson intervals are in the data table and CSV; they describe trial uncertainty for a fixed model. Seeds remain separate. Stripes mean pending, not zero error. Colors saturate at 50%; labels retain the measured values. All models train at nominal noise with the same 200,000-sequence, up-to-40-epoch protocol; off-nominal error reflects noise mismatch as well as capacity.

charts.title: LSTM size across the noise grid
charts.subtitle: 36/36 evaluated models · 2,196/2,196 model/settings · 1,024 trials per setting · snapshot 2026-11-18T09:47:07+00:00
charts.caption: Each cell averages P_L(50) equally across the 61 stationary noise settings. This descriptive grid mean is not expected error under a physical operating distribution, and is different from averaging error over rounds. Settings share random draws, so they are not 61 independent experiments. Seeds remain separate. Stripes mean pending, not zero error. Colors saturate at 50%; labels retain the measured values. All models train at nominal noise with the same 200,000-sequence, up-to-40-epoch protocol; off-nominal error reflects noise mismatch as well as capacity.

charts.title: Memory changes the baseline
charts.subtitle: E1 · 60,000 trials per decoder / seed · 50 rounds
charts.caption: Nominal noise: σq = 0.20L, σm = 0.05L, ρ = 0.9. Circles show fixed decoders with 95% Monte Carlo intervals; diamonds show three-seed LSTM means with seed min–max ranges. The two panels use different metrics. Lower is better.

charts.title: Correlation makes history useful
charts.subtitle: E2 · Two noise scales · Nine correlation settings
charts.caption: Shading is the min–max spread of three LSTM seeds, not a confidence band. Matched Bayes uses the true noise parameters at each point. The vertical scale is logarithmic above 0.001% and linear down to zero below it. Point estimates are connected as a visual guide.

charts.title: Performance depends on the noise regime
charts.subtitle: E3–E4 · Displacement and measurement-noise sweeps · ρ = 0.9
charts.caption: Same decoder definitions and seed bands as E2. Observed zeros are shown at zero on a scale that is linear below 0.001% and logarithmic above; zero observed errors do not establish zero risk. Sparse, separately trained matched-LSTM points are not included in these six-series sweeps.

charts.title: Revising past decisions matters
charts.subtitle: E1 ablations · Matched Bayes and the same LSTM checkpoint
charts.caption: This compares cumulative-parity decoding with per-round decisions. The LSTM comparison uses seed 0 for both heads; it does not compare the three-seed aggregate to a single-seed ablation. Bars show point estimates.

charts.title: Wrong assumptions can erase the gain
charts.subtitle: E5 · Model mismatch at the nominal point
charts.caption: Each cell is Bayes time-averaged error divided by nearest-lattice error on the same true noise model. Below 1× is better; above 1× is worse. True σq = 0.20L, σm = 0.05L, ρ = 0.9. The matched reference fills the ρ′ = 0.9, noise ×1 cell. This chart covers E5; E5b exists as a completed log, not a summary table.

charts.title: Learned decoding helps under structural mismatch
charts.subtitle: E6 · Two-regime switching noise · 20,000 trials per decoder / seed
charts.caption: Broad LSTM point estimates beat the fixed-model Bayesian baselines here, while regime-aware Bayes remains best. Circles use 95% normal Monte Carlo intervals; diamonds show three-seed means and seed min–max spread. This is a comparison within the switching model, not a claim about all nonstationary noise.

charts.title: Drift stress tests keep Bayes near the oracle
charts.subtitle: E9–E11 scenarios · Development random streams
charts.caption: These are development stress-test results, not the unfinished full E9–E11 evaluation. Runs use 2,000 trials × 1,000 rounds (IMM: 1,000 trials). ε is fitted before saturation. Ratios below 1 can arise from estimation noise and are not evidence of beating an exact oracle. Confidence intervals for ε ratios are not supplied.

charts.title: Bits per round determine the memory advantage
charts.subtitle: E14 · Ideal visibility and no readout flips · 4,000 trials × 200 rounds
charts.caption: The best sBs curve selects the lowest ε among the three tested δ values at each point; it is not an independently tuned policy. Analog and binary measurements carry different information. All bits in a round see the same displacement, so these are per-round comparisons, not equal-time hardware comparisons. The trained bit-LSTM is absent. All 120 E14 rows, including imperfect readout, are available in the data explorer.

charts.title: Fine corrections barely change logical error here
charts.subtitle: E15 · Closed-loop baselines · 20,000 trials × 200 rounds
charts.caption: Left: point estimates, with a linear region below 0.01% to show zero observations. Right: paired fine-minus-parity differences with ±1.96 SE; negative values favor fine correction. Zero errors were observed for both Bayesian policies at HW σm = 0.05L; this does not establish zero risk. DQN checkpoints and evaluated DQN rows are absent. The shift model omits finite-energy dissipation and ancilla back-action.

charts.title: Accuracy and throughput have different tradeoffs
charts.subtitle: Recorded cost benchmark · Accuracy and timing from the same runs
charts.caption: GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5080 Laptop GPU; PyTorch 2.11.0+cu128. Nearest lattice runs on CPU; other shown decoders use CUDA. Batches are 8,000 trials except IMM and window filters (2,000), all over 50 rounds. This is batched throughput, not single-stream feedback latency, and excludes training cost. The y-axis uses mean error rather than the potentially misleading long-run flip-rate metric. Timings were not remeasured on this machine.

charts.title: Exact-check summaries stay within two standard errors
charts.subtitle: Simulator validation rerun · Analytic references
charts.caption: The 15 plotted summaries cover exact single-round and flip formulas plus the maximum absolute z-score of the 50-round independent-noise decay check. The shaded interval is −2 to +2 standard errors. Approximate limiting checks are excluded from this exact-check plot. Agreement validates these simplified-model identities; it does not validate full hardware dynamics.

charts.title: Hardware-scale simulations occupy a different regime
charts.subtitle: Coverage benchmark · Snapshot before the E12 expansion
charts.caption: Each point is a simulated feature median, including the stars. Hardware-scale anchors use σq ≈ 0.072L and larger readout noise; ρ is assumed, not measured on a GKP device. This pre-E12 benchmark explains the coverage gap that motivated E12. It does not include the subsequent partial E12 evaluation or show experimental syndrome records.
